text:
Samir: FYI I'm starting a merge of CustA's LoRA adapter into base-7b-v2 so we can smoke-test on dedicated canary.
Igor: which adapter file and branch? share the eval pack you'll run.
Samir: adapter file is custA_lora_v1.pt on branch feat/custa-adapter. plan: lora-merge -> quant -> quick-eval pack 'custa_quick_eval_v3'.
Tess: did you run compatibility checks for vocab mismatch? last time a token offset caused hallucinations.
Samir: yep ran diff-vocab.py — mappings look identical, no special tokens. but need to confirm kv-cache layout and dtype after merge+quant.
Kai: heads-up: 8-bit quant on this adapter caused a regression in follow-up handling on previous customer. 4-bit + nf4 gave better latency and quality tradeoff.
Samir: interesting — I'll run both. initial merge command I'm using:

```
python infra/scripts/lora_merge.py \
  --base checkpoints/base-7b-v2.pt \
  --adapter checkpoints/custA_lora_v1.pt \
  --out /tmp/merged/custA-7b-v2-merged.pt \
  --merge-mode add
```

Samir: afterwards I run quantization like:

```
python infra/scripts/quantize.py \
  --in /tmp/merged/custA-7b-v2-merged.pt \
  --out /tmp/merged/custA-7b-v2-4bit.pt \
  --backend bitsandbytes --bits 4 --nf4
```

Tess: please add sha256 checksums + a small metadata JSON for dtype/layout. we had mismatches when deploy runtime expected torch.float16 keys and got float32.
Samir: will do.
Igor: for the quick-eval pack, remember to include both the customer scenario (+intent accuracy) and a control set for instruction-followups. we need per-case deltas.
Samir: first run results (unquantized merged):
- Intent Acc (custA subset): 0.873 -> +0.032 vs base
- Follow-up handling F1: 0.712 -> -0.018 vs base
- Avg latency (dedicated small batch): 84ms/token

Samir: after 4-bit quant (nf4):
- Intent Acc: 0.868 -> +0.027
- Follow-up F1: 0.706 -> -0.024
- Avg latency: 46ms/token

Samir: after 8-bit quant (bnb 8bit):
- Intent Acc: 0.860 -> +0.019
- Follow-up F1: 0.663 -> -0.067  <-- noticeable regression
- Avg latency: 52ms/token

Kai: that 8-bit follow-up drop is concerning. probably bnb 8bit interaction with rmsnorm/layernorm scaling.
Eva: can you attach example prompts where follow-up fails? need concrete traces for eval regression alerts.
Samir: adding two failing transcripts to the eval run output and linking here: https://artifacts.internal/runs/1764507890/custa-quick-eval
Tess: also check that merged KV cache ordering didn't shift. If adapter merge changed hidden-size or ordering we get off-by-one in attention.
Samir: verified model config (n_ctx, n_heads, d_model) is unchanged. ordering looks consistent.
Igor: proposed mitigation: for canary, keep runtime composition option (apply adapter at inference) instead of merging for the 8-bit path. That avoids destructive quantization interactions.
Samir: plan:
- push merged unquantized to canary slot A (runs in fp16)
- push merged 4-bit to canary slot B
- keep base+runtime-adapter on slot C using bnb8 to compare
- run custa_quick_eval_v3 across all three in parallel and collect per-route metrics

Samir: command to run eval (example):

```
python eval/run_eval.py \
  --pack eval/packs/custa_quick_eval_v3.yaml \
  --model /tmp/merged/custA-7b-v2-4bit.pt \
  --quant 4bit \
  --out results/1764507890/4bit
```

deploy-bot: Canary deployment initiated for route custa-canary-A -> model: /tmp/merged/custA-7b-v2.pt :rocket:
Eva: thanks — I'll create a short prompt set to focus on follow-up clarifications and edge-case ellipsis behavior.
Kai: if 4-bit still fails on follow-ups, we should escalate to infra/research. there may be a kernel-level issue or a merge-scaling bug.
Samir: noted. next steps: push artifacts (merged weights + sha256 + metadata), run parallel evals across the three slots, collect diffs, and prepare a short incident-style doc if follow-up F1 delta > 5pts.
Tess: ping me once results are in, I'll update the compatibility checklist and the onboarding playbook (docs/adapter_onboarding.md).
Samir: on it. will post final eval summary in this thread when complete. :thumbsup:
